clue.text: The part of the building bearing 135 degrees is for needlework

parts.note: a compass bearing of 135 degrees points south-east, abbreviated SE
a wing is a part of a large building jutting out from the main block

explanation.surface: A surveyor notes that one corner of a house, at a particular compass bearing, is the sewing room.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass bearing is written first even though the clue mentions the building part first; the charade is assembled in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitching with needle and thread is what needlework names, a general term for the craft.

clue.text: Japanese dish for American in his turn

indicators.note: the American goes inside the other piece
something turned is moved round, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: US, United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: A diner from the States orders Japanese food when it is his turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges HIS to SHI, and 'in' places US within it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegared rice with raw fish or vegetables is a classic Japanese food.

clue.text: Married at a shady spot in Southsea?

parts.note: to wed is to marry; wed is also the past tense
a dell is a small wooded hollow, a shady spot

explanation.surface: A couple got married in a shady corner of Southsea, the resort near Portsmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Southsea is a seaside district of Portsmouth, but here it is read as 'south sea': the Weddell Sea is part of the Southern Ocean off Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weddell Sea lies in the far south, off Antarctica, so it is a sea of the south.

clue.text: More opportunities for business with 16 14 6

definitions.meaning: the Suffolk racecourse that hosts the cross-referenced classic race for fillies

explanation.surface: A town gains extra business when it stages a famous horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket in Suffolk, the home of British horse racing, stages the 1,000 Guineas, one of the five classic races.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means an untapped trading outlet; as one, the Suffolk town with the famous racecourse.

clue.text: These years the times for proverbs?

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the years of the present era
ages are eras or periods of time

explanation.surface: A musing on whether today's era has given rise to its own proverbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sayings that express a common truth are both proverbs and adages; they are synonyms.

clue.text: County town of local engagement

definitions.meaning: the administrative town of the county of Derbyshire
a match between two nearby rival teams

explanation.surface: A county town is hosting a fixture between neighbouring sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby is also the name of the most famous classic horse race, run at Epsom, which ties it to the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the main town of Derbyshire, and a sporting contest between local rivals is called the same.

clue.text: Sanguine assumption that one will produce money

indicators.note: the run of words will bring forth, or yield up, letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: An optimistic person's belief that one investment is sure to make a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'Sanguine' and 'assumption'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British gold coins worth twenty-one shillings, so a form of money.

clue.text: Girl at men's party and nothing happening?

parts.note: a stag is a party for men only, as before a wedding
Nancy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman turns up at an all-male party where nothing much is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party, or stag night, is the British name for a bachelor party held before a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation, a state where activity has stopped, is what the word describes.

clue.text: Forest tree felled

parts.note: the ash is a common European tree
something felled has been brought down

explanation.surface: A woodland report: a tree has been cut down in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: ASHDOWN Forest is an area of heathland and woods in Sussex, in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue word is a capitalised proper name here: Ashdown Forest is a specific named woodland in East Sussex.

clue.text: Creative skill lives with an operative

parts.note: art is creative skill
is in the sense of exists or lives, as in 'he is'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a craftsman whose creative skill lives on in the work of a factory hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially a skilled manual one, which is what a craftsman is.

clue.text: Pay a quarter of the bill and hit the road with a pedal?

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay it

indicators.note: one letter of a four-letter word is a quarter of it, here its first letter
something hit is knocked about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone settles a share of the tab and leaves on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter of' takes the first of the four letters of 'bill', and 'hit' rearranges ROAD to OARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A footboard is a board for resting or pressing the feet on, which can serve as a treadle.

clue.text: Inorganic study brings setter's record into light

parts.note: the setter refers to themself; what belongs to the setter is 'mine'

indicators.note: brings one thing into another, so the record is placed inside the beam of light

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
a log is a written record, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that their notes bring some study of rocks and minerals into the light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts LOG inside RAY, giving RALOGY, after MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of minerals deals with non-living matter, so it is an inorganic field of study.

clue.text: Irish river and lough deserve to be proclaimed

indicators.note: a word proclaimed is spoken out, so the clue's word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to earn something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Praise for an Irish waterway, river and lake together, that merits being celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Erne flows through Northern Ireland and the Republic and forms Lough Erne, a large lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The Erne is a named river in Ireland that widens into the two Lough Erne lakes.

clue.text: Dr Who's character brings the valley a…

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England
the ellipsis runs on into the next clue: 'a' followed by its answer, a grand, which is abbreviated K

explanation.surface: A Dr Who monster turns up in a quiet valley, and the clue trails off mid-sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to the next: 'a… number' there is a grand, so this clue's last piece is K, the abbreviation for a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: The armoured alien villains of the BBC science-fiction series are among its best-known creatures.

clue.text: Fellow actors with the Queen in place for the 23

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
the cast is the set of actors in a play
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A university fellow and the actors of a play are joined by the monarch at a venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster in Yorkshire is where the St Leger, the race at 23, is run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yorkshire town's racecourse is the venue of that classic race each September.

clue.text: … number apostrophising the beach?

parts.note: to apostrophise is to address someone or something directly, in old style as 'thou'
a beach is made of sand

explanation.surface: A poet calls out to the seashore in old-fashioned style, as if counting grains.
explanation.walkthrough: Apostrophe here is the rhetorical figure of addressing an absent thing, as in 'O thou sand!'
explanation.definitionFit: It is a figure, ten hundreds, so a number.

clue.text: When the honour is affected it's time to strike

indicators.note: something affected is altered, so these letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: Industrial action is called the moment someone's dignity is slighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is affected' rearranges THE HONOUR. 'Strike' looks like a walkout, but it is a clock chiming.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock chimes at exactly o'clock, so the phrase marks the moment it sounds.

clue.text: Wooer not embarrassed by just a few

indicators.note: an embarrassed person is flustered and confused, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A suitor who is not embarrassed has only a handful of rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embarrassed' rearranges WOOER NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a small number, a couple or so, which is just a few.

clue.text: Yes, sort out potential jewel holders

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A jeweller agrees to sort out some cases for their gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges YES SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: These shellfish may hold pearls, so they may contain gems.

clue.text: Having viscosity and vulgarity

definitions.meaning: sticky, like paint that is not yet dry

explanation.surface: A description of something both gooey and in poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both slightly sticky to the touch and cheap or tasteless in style, two separate senses.

clue.text: Definitive number for girl — I have the same

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a lass is a girl
taken as written
the same number again, C repeated

explanation.surface: A girl swaps in for a number and another says they have the same one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' refers back to the first piece, so C appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A definitive, authoritative example is a standard one, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Female trees?

parts.note: read as wooden plants of the female sex, but meant as the classic flat race at Epsom open only to fillies, named after a tree

explanation.surface: A botanical question about whether some trees are female.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is one of England's five classic horse races, run at Epsom and restricted to three-year-old fillies, hence 'Female'.
explanation.definitionFit: The classic race for fillies takes its name from a plural of a common tree.

clue.text: Drug used by ethnic groups?

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
races are ethnic groups of people

explanation.surface: A grim note about narcotics use among certain communities.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the clue is wordplay only; the cross-references in other clues (19 21 across, the classic ones) tell you the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat or jump contests between galloping animals with jockeys are what the phrase names.

clue.text: Beast's satisfied comment about money

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: goes round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: 'ha!' is an exclamation of satisfaction
the yen is Japanese money

explanation.surface: An animal makes a pleased remark about cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts HA round YEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenging, dog-like African carnivore is a wild animal.

clue.text: Salty spot of 5 and 20

definitions.meaning: the place that gave its name to a bath salt, magnesium sulphate
the racecourse in Surrey where the two cross-referenced classic races are run

explanation.surface: A salty place that is home to two famous events.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom salts are named after the Surrey town; its downs host both the Derby (5) and the Oaks (20).
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey town is known for its mineral salts and as the course for the Derby and the Oaks.

clue.text: One of the 19 21 across where one member interrupts the rest rudely

indicators.note: breaks into the middle, so one piece is placed inside another
done rudely, roughly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a leg is one member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: Somewhere a single person cuts in impolitely while everyone else is talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' rearranges REST to STER, and 'interrupts' puts LEG inside it. The St Leger, run at Doncaster, is the oldest of the five English classic horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: The race run at Doncaster each September is one of England's five classic flat races.

clue.text: Be made up of expense infiltrated by heinous sin

indicators.note: one piece slips inside the other, as spies infiltrate an organisation

parts.note: cost is expense

indicators.note: a heinous act is wicked and twisted, so these letters are distorted

explanation.surface: A complaint that spending has been corrupted by some wicked wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heinous' rearranges SIN to NSI, and 'infiltrated by' puts it inside COST.
explanation.definitionFit: To comprise is to be composed of parts, the same as being made up of them.

clue.text: Return card (king or queen) of little weight

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
HM is His or Her Majesty, a king or queen

explanation.surface: Someone hands back a playing card, a monarch, which hardly weighs anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns CARD into DRAC, then HM follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A drachm is an old apothecaries' unit of weight, an eighth of an ounce, so a small measure.
